A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiMAC/AcT research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–E. The retained and added material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D–E report original LiMAC evaluations on AitW and AndroidControl, including accuracy, inference time, ablations, a confusion matrix, and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds failure-category and UI-element-count analyses in Appendices D.3–D.4.

M1.justification: The AcT architecture, input construction, contrastive click targeting, training objectives, and VLM routing remain unchanged. Changing 'ten' to 'eleven' action types in Sections 3.3–3.4 reconciles the description with the combined action vocabulary already listed in v1 Table 5; it does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use AndroidControl and the GoogleApps, Install, and WebShopping portions of AitW described in Appendix A. The new UI-element analysis stratifies existing observations without adding datasets, tasks, or input conditions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 and 6 retain the same Florence2, Qwen2-VL, T3A, M3A, SeeActchoice, and SeeActann comparators and their participation in module combinations. Newly cited research is not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The new diagnostic procedures categorize LiMAC/Florence2 failures by component and group prediction correctness into bins of ten UI elements, displaying only bins with more than five samples (D.3–D.4). Existing benchmark metrics, preprocessing, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds two targeted analyses: failure frequencies for action types, click targets, and input text, and prediction correctness versus UI-element count. These supplement the unchanged component ablations, confusion matrix, and case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new histograms report observation counts without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 6 are unchanged, including LiMAC/Florence2 accuracy of 72.2% on AitW and 63.1% on AndroidControl. New Figures 4–5 report error-category frequencies and correctness by UI-element count; the accompanying text reports a slight increase in failure rate with more elements. Section 3 newly reports VLM invocation for less than 15% of actions.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, input-sequence construction, and Equations 1–5 retain the same mathematical content, including cross-entropy and contrastive objectives. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The LiMAC/AcT contributions and principal efficiency and accuracy claims remain unchanged. Both abstracts retain the claimed improvements of up to 19% over fine-tuned VLMs and 42% over prompting baselines, while the introduction retains the up-to-30-times speedup claim.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly clarifies that lightweight inference entails a higher memory footprint from loading both models. Appendix D.4 attributes increased difficulty on crowded screens to harder target selection, and Section 6 identifies error handling and recovery as needed for robust online interactions.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds runtime documentation about VLM invocation frequency and the memory cost of loading AcT alongside the VLM. These are disclosures about the existing implementation; Appendix C's architecture, optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes, LoRA rank, and training epochs are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to SPA-Bench, DistRL, Li et al.'s 2020 UI-action work, and two studies of language models on mobile devices. Section 3.1 also explicitly relates UI-element embeddings to earlier work and identifies vision-encoder fine-tuning as a distinction, providing a focused expansion of positioning.

P1.justification: Local revisions streamline the abstract and transformer background, clarify evaluation prose, and correct the combined action count. Appendix D is renamed and divided into D.1–D.4; affiliations and acknowledgements are updated. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds error-frequency and UI-element-count plots as Figures 4–5, adds dataset-membership columns to Table 5, and adjusts figure sizing, captions, and headers. The existing case-study images are retained and renumbered from Figures 4–5 to Figures 6–7.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity by correcting the action-count inconsistency, explaining the compute-versus-memory tradeoff, and better acknowledging related UI representations. The new appendix analyses provide useful descriptive evidence about failure patterns and UI complexity. These are incremental gains in transparency and diagnostic insight; the central method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
